properties.decision:
DECIDED by Anthony 2026-08-05, taking OPTION (c) from the options this node recorded while open. The measurement below is unchanged; what follows it is the choice and what it does not cover.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED IT, from the first real trial of cap:corpus-ingest over six dev_storyflow architecture documents. `dynograph_resolution::token_sort_ratio` against the auto-merge threshold of 90:

  95  dynograph-vector   vs dynograph-core        <- SILENTLY MERGED, WRONG
  94  dynograph-storage  vs dynograph-core        <- SILENTLY MERGED, WRONG
  93  dynograph-extract  vs dynograph-context     <- SILENTLY MERGED, WRONG
  91  dynograph-server   vs dynograph-query       <- SILENTLY MERGED, WRONG
  84  Auth Service       vs Authentication Service (NOT merged — and this is the case the feature EXISTS for)

ONE DOCUMENT DECLARING NINE CRATES PRODUCED FIVE NODES. 44% of an architecture destroyed silently, and the survivors asserted something FALSE rather than merely being incomplete: `cmp:dynograph-core` carried the name "dynograph-storage".

WHY NO THRESHOLD REPAIRS IT, which is the reason (a) was rejected: 95 was a sibling pair and 84 a true duplicate, so the ORDERING is inverted and no cutoff separates them. `docs/scope-corpus-ingest.md` asserted "90 on a token-sorted ratio is near-identity"; measured, that is false for the names real systems use.

THE CHOICE — A DIFFERENT QUESTION, NOT A BETTER NUMBER. Before auto-merging, both names are tokenised on every non-alphanumeric (deliberately NOT `name_tokens`, which splits on whitespace and so cannot see inside `dynograph-core`). A merge is REFUSED when either side carries a whole word the other does not ABBREVIATE. "core" and "storage" are not spellings of each other; "auth" and "authentication" are, with a three-character minimum because below that almost anything prefixes anything. An unpaired extra word is distinguishing too, so `Auth Service` and `Auth Service v2` stay apart — the case the scope doc warned collapsing would lose. Reordered tokens still converge, so BL-186's ordering fix is untouched.

AND THE REFUSAL SAYS WHICH WORD DID IT. `MergeCandidate.distinguished_by` carries e.g. "`storage` has no counterpart in \"dynograph-core\"". "These two were not merged" is not something a person can rule on; naming the word is. `None` means the score simply fell short, which needs no explanation.

THE SECOND FIX IN THE SAME CHANGE: `CorpusReport.fuzzy_merges` was a `usize` for one day and is now `Vec<CorpusMerge>`, each entry carrying the DOCUMENT that caused it — which the single-document report structurally cannot know. A merge is the one thing an ingest does WITHOUT ASKING and cannot undo by re-running, and the aggregate had reduced it to a number at exactly the scale where that matters most.

VERIFIED, AND MUTATION-CHECKED: `tests/sibling_merge.rs` pins nine crates staying nine, an abbreviation still merging, a version suffix staying apart, reordered tokens still converging, and the refusal naming its word. Disabling the discriminator returns 5-of-9 and fails exactly the three tests that name those properties while leaving the two that should be insensitive passing. Re-run against the real dev_storyflow document that found it: 9 of 9 crates survive, each with its own name.

⭐ WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT REMAINS: the destructive direction is handled; the MISSING direction is untouched. `Read Cache` ~ `Local Store` is still invisible — not a low score, no score at all — so two documents that RENAMED the same thing still produce two nodes. This decision makes the lexical pass safe, not sufficient. `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` is where that half lives, and this trial is the strongest evidence yet for it: the lexical signal here was not merely weak, it was INVERTED, which is the argument a semantic tiebreaker has been waiting for.

ALSO NOT SETTLED: the ask band is still noisy. The same trial's eleven merge candidates were ELEVEN OUT OF ELEVEN FALSE POSITIVES. The discriminator now labels the sibling ones, which should make them skimmable rather than gruelling, but nobody has measured the band again since.

STILL NOT MEASURED, and it bounds every number above: what this does across the other 1,118 documents. The trial was SIX documents chosen for topical overlap; 44% is one document's crate list, not a corpus-wide rate.
properties.name: DECIDED — a merge needs a discriminator, not a threshold: siblings are held apart by whole-word difference
properties.rationale:
Moved to accepted on Anthony's explicit instruction ("fix the fuzzy_merges regression, then the token discriminator"), which chose option (c) over the four alternatives this node had recorded.

The measurement is kept in full rather than trimmed to the conclusion, because the numbers are what make the fix defensible and what would otherwise be re-derived: "fuzzy matching is too aggressive" decays into folklore within a session, and "95 for a sibling pair, 84 for a true duplicate" does not.

Two things are deliberately recorded as NOT fixed — the missing-convergence direction and the noisy ask band — so this does not read as having closed the resolution question. It closed the destructive half of it. The one that remains is the one that needs embeddings, and saying so here is what stops the next session treating lexical resolution as done.
